## Get-PoshUIConfiguration

Gets the resolved PoshUI startup configuration

### Syntax

```powershell
Get-PoshUIConfiguration [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Returns an independent snapshot of the active module-owned settings.
Runtime mode and feature toggles remain explicit process inputs, while
theme and component settings stay in module scope.

### Inputs

- None.

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Get-PoshUIConfiguration
```

Returns every resolved configuration section.

#### Example 2

```powershell
(Get-PoshUIConfiguration).Progress.Width
```

Returns the resolved progress width.

#### Example 3

```powershell
(Get-PoshUIConfiguration).Theme.Component.Table
```

Returns the active table component tokens.

### Notes

POSH_UI_MODE remains a process-level runtime switch and is resolved by
Get-PoshUIRuntime rather than this startup snapshot.

## Get-PoshUIRuntime

Gets the active PoshUI terminal capabilities

### Syntax

```powershell
Get-PoshUIRuntime [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Resolves the current runtime mode and explains why it was selected.
The returned value reports redirection, interactive-input, color, and
terminal-control capabilities without changing terminal state.

### Inputs

- None.

### Outputs

- PoshUI.Runtime.

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Get-PoshUIRuntime
```

Returns the current runtime capabilities.

#### Example 2

```powershell
(Get-PoshUIRuntime).Reason
```

Explains why auto mode selected rich or plain output.

#### Example 3

```powershell
$env:POSH_UI_MODE = 'off'; Get-PoshUIRuntime
```

Confirms that display and logging effects are disabled.

### Notes

POSH_UI_MODE accepts auto, rich, plain, or off. Auto mode also honors
CI, redirected streams, TERM=dumb, and NO_COLOR.

## New-PoshUITheme

Creates an independent layered PoshUI theme

### Syntax

```powershell
New-PoshUITheme [[-Name] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Creates primitive, semantic, and component token maps for one of the
built-in themes. The returned object is independent of the active
configuration and can be changed by a caller without mutating another
theme or the process environment.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Name` | `String` | No | 1 | No | unanet | Built-in theme name. The default is unanet. |

### Inputs

- None.

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
New-PoshUITheme
```

Creates the dark theme.

#### Example 2

```powershell
$theme = New-PoshUITheme -Name unanet
```

Creates an independent Unanet theme.

#### Example 3

```powershell
(New-PoshUITheme -Name light).Component.Table.Header
```

Returns the light theme's table-header token.

### Notes

Theme tokens are mode-neutral ANSI values. Formatting and display
commands apply the active runtime mode when producing output.

## Set-PoshUITheme

Sets the active PoshUI theme

### Syntax

```powershell
Set-PoshUITheme [[-Name] <string>] [-PassThru] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
Set-PoshUITheme -Theme <Theme> [-PassThru] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Activates a built-in or caller-supplied theme for subsequent rich-mode
rendering. PoshUI copies custom themes before activation, so later
caller mutations cannot change module behavior. Plain and off modes
continue to remove all theme control sequences.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Name` | `String` | No | 1 | No | unanet | Built-in theme name. The default is unanet. |
| `-Theme` | `PSObject` | Yes | named | true (ByValue) |  | Custom PoshUI.Theme created by New-PoshUITheme and modified by the caller. |
| `-PassThru` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Returns an independent copy of the active theme. |
| `-WhatIf` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No |  |  |
| `-Confirm` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No |  |  |

### Inputs

- PoshUI.Theme.

### Outputs

- PoshUI.Theme when PassThru is supplied. Otherwise none.

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Set-PoshUITheme
```

Activates the default Unanet theme.

#### Example 2

```powershell
Set-PoshUITheme -Name dark -PassThru
```

Activates and returns a copy of the dark theme.

#### Example 3

```powershell
$theme = New-PoshUITheme -Name unanet
$theme.Component.Box.Border = "`e[38;2;82;214;255m"
$theme | Set-PoshUITheme
```

Activates a customized independent theme.

### Notes

Theme state is local to the imported PoshUI module instance and is not
written to the process environment.

## Set-PoshUILogConfiguration

Updates the PoshUI application logging configuration

### Syntax

```powershell
Set-PoshUILogConfiguration [[-Level] <string>] [[-FilePath] <string>] [[-ConsoleOutput] <bool>] [[-MaximumSize] <long>] [[-MaximumFiles] <int>] [-PassThru] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Updates only the supplied settings for terminal output and the optional
synchronous JSONL file sink. A non-empty file path enables the sink and
creates its parent directory. An empty path disables file output.
Configuration is held in module scope and does not mutate environment
variables.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Level` | `String` | No | 1 | No |  | Minimum accepted level: Debug, Info, Warning, Error, or Fatal. |
| `-FilePath` | `String` | No | 2 | No |  | JSONL file path. An empty value disables the file sink. |
| `-ConsoleOutput` | `Boolean` | No | 3 | No | False | Whether accepted events are also rendered to the terminal. |
| `-MaximumSize` | `Int64` | No | 4 | No | 0 | Maximum active-file size in bytes before the next event rotates it. |
| `-MaximumFiles` | `Int32` | No | 5 | No | 0 | Number of numbered archive files retained beside the active file. |
| `-PassThru` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Returns a copy of the resulting configuration. |
| `-WhatIf` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No |  |  |
| `-Confirm` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No |  |  |

### Inputs

- None.

### Outputs

- PoshUI.LogConfiguration when PassThru is supplied. Otherwise none.

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Set-PoshUILogConfiguration -Level Info -FilePath ./logs/app.jsonl
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
Set-PoshUILogConfiguration -ConsoleOutput $false -MaximumSize 5MB
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
Set-PoshUILogConfiguration -FilePath '' -PassThru
```

## Write-PoshUILog

Writes one structured PoshUI application log event

### Syntax

```powershell
Write-PoshUILog [-Level] <string> [-Message] <string> [-Data <IDictionary>] [-Exception <Exception>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Creates one event, applies level filtering, renders a human-readable
terminal line when enabled, and appends one compact JSON object to the
configured local file sink. Fatal is a severity level and never exits
the caller. Off mode suppresses both destinations.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Level` | `String` | Yes | 1 | No |  | Event severity: Debug, Info, Warning, Error, or Fatal. |
| `-Message` | `String` | Yes | 2 | No |  | Human-readable event message. Terminal control sequences are removed. |
| `-Data` | `IDictionary` | No | named | No |  | Optional structured fields serialized verbatim beneath the data<br>property. Do not include passwords, tokens, or other credentials. |
| `-Exception` | `Exception` | No | named | No |  | Optional exception serialized as type, message, and stackTrace fields. |

### Inputs

- None.

### Outputs

- None.

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Write-PoshUILog -Level Info -Message 'Deployment started'
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
Write-PoshUILog -Level Warning -Message 'Slow health check' -Data @{ seconds = 12 }
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
Write-PoshUILog -Level Error -Message 'Promotion failed' -Exception $_.Exception
```

## Clear-PoshUILog

Clears the active PoshUI JSONL file sink

### Syntax

```powershell
Clear-PoshUILog [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Truncates the configured active file when it exists. It does not remove
rotated archives and has no effect when the sink is disabled, missing,
or PoshUI is off.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-WhatIf` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No |  |  |
| `-Confirm` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No |  |  |

### Inputs

- None.

### Outputs

- None.

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Clear-PoshUILog
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
Set-PoshUILogConfiguration -FilePath ./logs/app.jsonl; Clear-PoshUILog
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
$env:POSH_UI_MODE = 'off'; Clear-PoshUILog
```

## New-PoshUIProgress

Creates an independent progress model

### Syntax

```powershell
New-PoshUIProgress [-Total] <int> [[-Current] <int>] [[-Label] <string>] [[-Width] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Creates an in-memory progress model with its own total, current value,
label, width, start time, and rendering characters. The model has no
terminal side effects and can be updated independently of other models.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Total` | `Int32` | Yes | 1 | No | 0 | Total number of work units. Must be at least one. |
| `-Current` | `Int32` | No | 2 | No | 0 | Initial completed work units. Values above Total are clamped to Total. |
| `-Label` | `String` | No | 3 | No | Progress | Text displayed beside the progress bar. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | 4 | No | [int]$script:PO_PROGRESS_CONFIGURATION.Progress.Width | Number of terminal columns used by the bar body. Defaults to the<br>resolved startup configuration. |

### Inputs

- None.

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
New-PoshUIProgress -Total 10
```

Creates a ten-unit progress model.

#### Example 2

```powershell
New-PoshUIProgress -Total 100 -Current 25 -Label 'Build'
```

Creates a build progress model at 25 percent.

#### Example 3

```powershell
$progress = New-PoshUIProgress -Total 4 -Width 10
PS> $progress | Update-PoshUIProgress -Increment 1
```

Creates and updates one independent model.

### Notes

Use Format-PoshUIProgress for effect-free rendering and
Show-PoshUIProgress for terminal output.

## Update-PoshUIProgress

Updates an independent progress model

### Syntax

```powershell
Update-PoshUIProgress [-Progress] <psobject> [[-Increment] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Adds an increment to the supplied progress model and clamps the result
between zero and the model total. The same model is returned for
continued pipeline composition.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Progress` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | Progress model created by New-PoshUIProgress. |
| `-Increment` | `Int32` | No | 2 | No | 1 | Signed number of units to add. The default is one. |

### Inputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Update-PoshUIProgress -Progress $progress
```

Advances the model by one unit.

#### Example 2

```powershell
$progress | Update-PoshUIProgress -Increment 5
```

Advances a pipeline model by five units.

#### Example 3

```powershell
$progress | Update-PoshUIProgress -Increment -1 | Format-PoshUIProgress
```

Moves the model back one unit and formats it.

### Notes

This command mutates only the supplied in-memory model.

## Format-PoshUIProgress

Formats a progress model without terminal effects

### Syntax

```powershell
Format-PoshUIProgress [-Progress] <psobject> [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Returns one progress line for the supplied model. It does not write to
the host, move the cursor, or mutate the model.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Progress` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | Progress model created by New-PoshUIProgress. |

### Inputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Outputs

- System.String

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Format-PoshUIProgress -Progress $progress
```

Returns the formatted progress line.

#### Example 2

```powershell
$line = $progress | Format-PoshUIProgress
```

Captures the line without displaying it.

#### Example 3

```powershell
@($first, $second) | Format-PoshUIProgress
```

Formats two independent models for composition.

### Notes

Rendering uses the characters captured when the model was created.

## Show-PoshUIProgress

Displays a formatted progress model

### Syntax

```powershell
Show-PoshUIProgress [-Progress] <psobject> [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Formats the supplied model and writes it through the PoshUI runtime
boundary. Interactive terminals receive an in-place carriage-return
update. Plain terminals receive a stable line, and off mode writes
nothing.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Progress` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | Progress model created by New-PoshUIProgress. |

### Inputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Outputs

- None.

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Show-PoshUIProgress -Progress $progress
```

Displays the current model state.

#### Example 2

```powershell
$progress | Show-PoshUIProgress
```

Displays a pipeline model.

#### Example 3

```powershell
$progress | Update-PoshUIProgress | Show-PoshUIProgress
```

Advances and displays the model.

### Notes

Use Format-PoshUIProgress when the caller needs composable output.

## Format-PoshUIBox

Formats a terminal box as composable text lines.

### Syntax

```powershell
Format-PoshUIBox [[-Title] <string>] [[-Content] <string[]>] [-Color <string>] [-Width <int>] [-Style <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Creates a standard, rounded, or double-line box without writing to the
host or changing terminal state. In plain runtime mode, ANSI control
sequences are removed from the returned strings.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Title` | `String` | No | 1 | No |  | The optional title centered in the box header. |
| `-Content` | `String[]` | No | 2 | true (ByValue) | @() | The content lines to place inside the box. Content can be supplied from<br>the pipeline. |
| `-Color` | `String` | No | named | No | $script:PoshUIStyle.BoxBorder | An optional ANSI color sequence applied to the box borders. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | named | No | $script:PoshUIBoxDefaultWidth | The total display width of the box, including its borders. |
| `-Style` | `String` | No | named | No | Standard | The border style: Standard, Rounded, or Double. |

### Outputs

- System.String

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Format-PoshUIBox -Title 'Status' -Content 'Ready' -Width 24
```

Returns each rendered box row as a separate string.

#### Example 2

```powershell
'One', 'Two' | Format-PoshUIBox -Title 'Items' -Style Rounded
```

Collects pipeline input and returns one rounded box.

#### Example 3

```powershell
Format-PoshUIBox -Content 'Warning' -Style Double | Set-Content box.txt
```

Saves a double-line box without writing directly to the host.

## Show-PoshUIBox

Displays a terminal box through the PoshUI runtime boundary.

### Syntax

```powershell
Show-PoshUIBox [[-Title] <string>] [[-Content] <string[]>] [-Color <string>] [-Width <int>] [-Style <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Formats a box with Format-PoshUIBox and writes each line through
Write-PoshUIHost. Runtime modes therefore control color, redirection, and
disabled output consistently with the rest of PoshUI.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Title` | `String` | No | 1 | No |  | The optional title centered in the box header. |
| `-Content` | `String[]` | No | 2 | true (ByValue) | @() | The content lines to display. Content can be supplied from the pipeline. |
| `-Color` | `String` | No | named | No | $script:PoshUIStyle.BoxBorder | An optional ANSI color sequence applied to the box borders. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | named | No | $script:PoshUIBoxDefaultWidth | The total display width of the box, including its borders. |
| `-Style` | `String` | No | named | No | Standard | The border style: Standard, Rounded, or Double. |

### Outputs

- None

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Show-PoshUIBox -Title 'Status' -Content 'Ready' -Width 24
```

Displays a standard box through the configured runtime.

#### Example 2

```powershell
'One', 'Two' | Show-PoshUIBox -Title 'Items' -Style Rounded
```

Collects pipeline input and displays one rounded box.

#### Example 3

```powershell
Show-PoshUIBox -Content 'Warning' -Style Double
```

Displays a double-line box through the configured runtime.

## New-PoshUITable

| `-Header` | `String[]` | No | 2 | No | @() | Sets the initial column headers. |
| `-Padding` | `Int32` | No | 3 | No | [int]$script:PoshUITableConfiguration.Padding | Sets the number of spaces on each side of a cell value. |

#### Example 1

```powershell
$table = New-PoshUITable -Style Rounded -Header Name, Status
```

#### Example 2

#### Example 3


## Add-PoshUITableRow

Adds values or pipeline objects to a PoshUI table.

### Syntax

```powershell
Add-PoshUITableRow [-Table] <Table> [-Values] <Object[]> [-PassThru] [<CommonParameters>]
Add-PoshUITableRow [-Table] <Table> -InputObject <psobject> [-Property <string[]>] [-PassThru] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Adds one row for each invocation. In the Values parameter set, each value
becomes a cell. In the InputObject parameter set, properties are projected
in the requested order, or in header order when Property is omitted.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Table` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | No |  | The table returned by New-PoshUITable. |
| `-Values` | `Object[]` | Yes | 2 | No |  | The ordered cell values for one row. |
| `-InputObject` | `PSObject` | Yes | named | true (ByValue) |  | An object received from the pipeline or supplied directly. |
| `-Property` | `String[]` | No | named | No |  | Property names to project from InputObject. Defaults to the table headers. |
| `-PassThru` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Returns the updated table instance. |

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Add-PoshUITableRow -Table $table -Values 'api', 'healthy'
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
$services | Add-PoshUITableRow -Table $table -Property Name, Status
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
Add-PoshUITableRow -Table $table -Values 'worker', 'queued' -PassThru
```

## Format-PoshUIHorizontalBarChart

Formats a horizontal bar chart as composable text lines.

### Syntax

```powershell
Format-PoshUIHorizontalBarChart [[-Title] <string>] [-Data] <double[]> [[-Labels] <string[]>] [[-Width] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Creates a horizontal bar chart without writing to the host. In rich mode,
the returned strings contain the configured ANSI colors. In plain and off
modes, ANSI sequences are removed. The strings can be captured, composed,
redirected, or passed to Show-PoshUIHorizontalBarChart.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Title` | `String` | No | 1 | No |  | An optional title written above the chart. |
| `-Data` | `Double[]` | Yes | 2 | No |  | One or more numeric values to chart. |
| `-Labels` | `String[]` | No | 3 | No | @() | Optional labels corresponding to the data values. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | 4 | No | 50 | The maximum bar width in terminal cells. |

### Outputs

- System.String

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Format-PoshUIHorizontalBarChart -Title 'Builds' -Data 2, 4 -Labels 'Failed', 'Passed' -Width 10
```

Returns the title, a blank line, and two formatted bar lines.

#### Example 2

```powershell
Format-PoshUIHorizontalBarChart -Data 5, 8 -Width 20 | Set-Content chart.txt
```

Saves an unlabeled chart without writing directly to the host.

#### Example 3

```powershell
$lines = Format-PoshUIHorizontalBarChart -Data 1, 2, 3 -Labels A, B, C
```

Captures the formatted chart lines for composition.

## Format-PoshUISparkline

Formats numeric data as a composable sparkline string.

### Syntax

```powershell
Format-PoshUISparkline [-Data] <double[]> [[-Levels] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Scales numeric values across the configured spark glyphs and returns one
string without writing to the host. The result is suitable for embedding in
tables, boxes, status lines, or other formatted output.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Data` | `Double[]` | Yes | 1 | No |  | One or more numeric values to represent. |
| `-Levels` | `Int32` | No | 2 | No | 8 | The number of spark glyph levels to use, from two through eight. |

### Outputs

- System.String

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Format-PoshUISparkline -Data 1, 2, 3, 4
```

Returns a four-character sparkline.

#### Example 2

```powershell
$trend = Format-PoshUISparkline -Data 8, 5, 7 -Levels 4
```

Captures a sparkline using four glyph levels.

#### Example 3

```powershell
"Latency: $(Format-PoshUISparkline -Data 10, 12, 9)"
```

Composes the returned sparkline into another string.


### Description

| `-Levels` | `Int32` | No | 2 | No | 8 | The number of spark glyph levels to use, from two through eight. |
| `-Newline` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Writes a trailing newline after the sparkline. |

### Outputs

- None

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Show-PoshUISparkline -Data 4, 3, 6, 8
```

Displays an inline four-character sparkline.

#### Example 2

```powershell
Show-PoshUISparkline -Data 4, 3, 6, 8 -Newline
```

Displays a sparkline followed by a newline.

#### Example 3

```powershell
Show-PoshUISparkline -Data 1, 5, 3 -Levels 4
```

Displays a sparkline using four glyph levels.

### Syntax

- System.Object


## Read-PoshUIText

Reads validated text from an interactive terminal

### Syntax

```powershell
Read-PoshUIText [-Message] <string> [-Default <string>] [-Validator <scriptblock>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Reads one line, applies an optional scriptblock validator, and returns
the accepted text. Redirected input returns an explicit default or
throws instead of blocking.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Message` | `String` | Yes | 1 | No |  | Prompt shown before reading input. |
| `-Default` | `String` | No | named | No |  | Value returned for empty or redirected input. |
| `-Validator` | `ScriptBlock` | No | named | No |  | Scriptblock that receives the candidate text and returns a Boolean. |

### Inputs

- None.

### Outputs

- System.String.

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Read-PoshUIText -Message 'Service name'
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
Read-PoshUIText -Message 'Region' -Default east
```

#### Example 3


## Read-PoshUIPassword

Reads a password without exposing plaintext

### Syntax

```powershell
Read-PoshUIPassword [-Message] <string> [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Reads masked key input into a read-only SecureString. Escape or Ctrl+C
cancels and returns no value. Redirected input throws instead of blocking.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Message` | `String` | Yes | 1 | No |  | Prompt shown before reading the password. |

### Inputs

- None.

### Outputs

- System.Security.SecureString.

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Read-PoshUIPassword -Message 'Password'
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
$secret = Read-PoshUIPassword 'Artifactory token'
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
$credential = [PSCredential]::new('user', (Read-PoshUIPassword 'Token'))
```

## Confirm-PoshUIChoice

Reads a yes or no confirmation

### Syntax

```powershell
Confirm-PoshUIChoice [-Message] <string> [-Default <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

Returns a Boolean response from an interactive terminal. Noninteractive
calls return false so automation never grants confirmation implicitly.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Message` | `String` | Yes | 1 | No |  | Confirmation question. |
| `-Default` | `String` | No | named | No | Yes | Response used when Enter is pressed without text. |

### Inputs

- None.

### Outputs

- System.Boolean.

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Confirm-PoshUIChoice -Message 'Continue?'
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
Confirm-PoshUIChoice -Message 'Delete file?' -Default No
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
if (Confirm-PoshUIChoice 'Deploy?') { 'approved' }
```

## Format-PoshUIText

Formats text within a terminal-width-aware rectangular area.

### Syntax

```powershell
Format-PoshUIText [-InputObject] <Object> [[-Width] <int>] [-PaddingLeft <int>] [-PaddingRight <int>] [-PaddingTop <int>] [-PaddingBottom <int>] [-HorizontalAlignment <string>] [-Overflow <string>] [-Ellipsis <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Wraps or truncates input, applies horizontal alignment and padding, and
returns fixed-width lines without writing to the terminal.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-InputObject` | `Object` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | Text or formatted component lines to arrange. Pipeline input is accepted. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | 2 | No | 0 | Output width. Zero resolves the current terminal width with an 80-column fallback. |
| `-PaddingLeft` | `Int32` | No | named | No | 0 | Blank columns added at the left edge. |
| `-PaddingRight` | `Int32` | No | named | No | 0 | Blank columns added at the right edge. |
| `-PaddingTop` | `Int32` | No | named | No | 0 | Blank lines added above the content. |
| `-PaddingBottom` | `Int32` | No | named | No | 0 | Blank lines added below the content. |
| `-HorizontalAlignment` | `String` | No | named | No | Left | Left, Center, or Right alignment within the content area. |
| `-Overflow` | `String` | No | named | No | Wrap | Wrap long input onto more lines or truncate it with Ellipsis. |
| `-Ellipsis` | `String` | No | named | No | … | Marker used when Overflow is Truncate. |

### Outputs

- System.String

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Format-PoshUIText -InputObject 'ready' -Width 9 -HorizontalAlignment Center
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
'alpha beta' | Format-PoshUIText -Width 6 -Overflow Wrap
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
Format-PoshUIText 'deployment' -Width 6 -Overflow Truncate -Ellipsis '...'
```

## Format-PoshUIPanel

Formats content inside a terminal-width-aware panel.

### Syntax

```powershell
Format-PoshUIPanel [-InputObject] <Object> [-Title <string>] [-Width <int>] [-Padding <int>] [-HorizontalAlignment <string>] [-Overflow <string>] [-BorderStyle <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Builds a complete panel render model before returning its border and content lines.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-InputObject` | `Object` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | Text or formatted component lines placed inside the panel. |
| `-Title` | `String` | No | named | No |  | Optional panel title displayed in the top border. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | named | No | 0 | Total panel width. Zero resolves the terminal width. |
| `-Padding` | `Int32` | No | named | No | 1 | Horizontal padding inside the panel. |
| `-HorizontalAlignment` | `String` | No | named | No | Left | Content alignment inside the panel. |
| `-Overflow` | `String` | No | named | No | Wrap | Wrap or Truncate behavior for content wider than the panel. |
| `-BorderStyle` | `String` | No | named | No | Rounded | Rounded, Square, Ascii, or None. |

## New-PoshUIDataColumn

Creates a typed object-table column definition

### Syntax

```powershell
New-PoshUIDataColumn [-Property] <string> [[-Name] <string>] [[-Formatter] <scriptblock>] [[-MaxWidth] <int>] [[-Overflow] <string>] [[-Alignment] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Creates an independent column definition for Format-PoshUIDataTable. A
column selects one object property and can apply its own formatter, maximum
width, overflow behavior, and alignment. It does not read or change global
table state.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Property` | `String` | Yes | 1 | No |  | Property name read from each pipeline object. |
| `-Name` | `String` | No | 2 | No | $Property | Header label. Defaults to Property. |
| `-Formatter` | `ScriptBlock` | No | 3 | No |  | Script block invoked with the property value and source object. |
| `-MaxWidth` | `Int32` | No | 4 | No | 0 | Maximum rendered width. Zero uses the table-level maximum. |
| `-Overflow` | `String` | No | 5 | No | Truncate | Wrap preserves all text on continuation rows. Truncate uses an ellipsis. |
| `-Alignment` | `String` | No | 6 | No | Left | Cell alignment within the resolved column width. |

### Inputs

- None

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
New-PoshUIDataColumn -Property Name
```

Creates a column whose label and property are Name.

#### Example 2

```powershell
New-PoshUIDataColumn -Property Duration -Name Seconds -Formatter { param($value) '{0:N2}' -f $value }
```

Creates a calculated presentation for Duration.

#### Example 3

```powershell
New-PoshUIDataColumn -Property Notes -MaxWidth 20 -Overflow Wrap
```

Creates a wrapping Notes column.

### Notes

Column definitions are immutable by convention and safe to reuse.

## Format-PoshUIDataTable

Formats pipeline objects as a structured data table

### Syntax

```powershell
Format-PoshUIDataTable [-InputObject] <Object> [[-Property] <Object[]>] [[-SortBy] <string>] [[-Page] <int>] [[-PageSize] <int>] [[-MaxColumnWidth] <int>] [[-Overflow] <string>] [-Descending] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Buffers pipeline objects, selects properties without delimiter encoding,
optionally sorts and pages them, and returns plain composable text lines.
Embedded delimiters remain cell data and embedded newlines become visual
continuation rows. This command never writes to the host.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-InputObject` | `Object` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | Objects to render. Accepts pipeline input. |
| `-Property` | `Object[]` | No | 2 | No |  | Property names or PoshUI.DataColumn definitions. Omitted, properties are<br>inferred from the first object. |
| `-SortBy` | `String` | No | 3 | No |  | Property used to sort before paging. |
| `-Descending` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Sorts descending instead of ascending. |
| `-Page` | `Int32` | No | 4 | No | 1 | One-based page number. |
| `-PageSize` | `Int32` | No | 5 | No | 0 | Rows per page. Zero disables paging. |
| `-MaxColumnWidth` | `Int32` | No | 6 | No | 40 | Default maximum width for columns without their own maximum. |
| `-Overflow` | `String` | No | 7 | No | Truncate | Default overflow behavior for property-name columns. |

### Inputs

- System.Object

### Outputs

- System.String

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Get-Process | Select-Object -First 5 | Format-PoshUIDataTable -Property Name, Id
```

Formats process names and identifiers.

#### Example 2

```powershell
$notes = New-PoshUIDataColumn -Property Notes -MaxWidth 12 -Overflow Wrap
$items | Format-PoshUIDataTable -Property Name, $notes
```

Wraps the Notes column while preserving embedded newlines.

#### Example 3

```powershell
$items | Format-PoshUIDataTable -Property Name, Score -SortBy Score -Descending -Page 2 -PageSize 10
```

Returns the second page after descending score sort.

### Notes

Rendering uses an ASCII border so redirected output is stable.

## Show-PoshUIDataTable

Displays pipeline objects as a structured data table

### Syntax

```powershell
Show-PoshUIDataTable [-InputObject] <Object> [[-Property] <Object[]>] [[-SortBy] <string>] [[-Page] <int>] [[-PageSize] <int>] [[-MaxColumnWidth] <int>] [[-Overflow] <string>] [-Descending] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Applies the Format-PoshUIDataTable contract and writes each resulting line
through the shared PoshUI host boundary. Off mode suppresses host effects.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |

| `-Property` | `Object[]` | No | 2 | No |  | Property names or PoshUI.DataColumn definitions. |
| `-SortBy` | `String` | No | 3 | No |  | Property used to sort before paging. |
| `-Descending` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Sorts descending. |
| `-Page` | `Int32` | No | 4 | No | 1 | One-based page number. |
| `-PageSize` | `Int32` | No | 5 | No | 0 | Rows per page. Zero disables paging. |
| `-MaxColumnWidth` | `Int32` | No | 6 | No | 40 | Default maximum column width. |
| `-Overflow` | `String` | No | 7 | No | Truncate | Default overflow behavior. |

### Inputs

- System.Object

### Outputs

- None

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
$items | Show-PoshUIDataTable -Property Name, State
```

Displays two selected properties.

#### Example 2

```powershell
$items | Show-PoshUIDataTable -Property Name, Notes -Overflow Wrap -MaxColumnWidth 20
```

Displays wrapped values.

#### Example 3

```powershell
$items | Show-PoshUIDataTable -Property Name -Page 1 -PageSize 25
```

Displays the first page.

### Notes

This is the effectful wrapper for Format-PoshUIDataTable.

## Format-PoshUITree

Formats nested objects and collections as a hierarchy

### Syntax

```powershell
Format-PoshUITree [-InputObject] <Object> [[-RootLabel] <string>] [[-Style] <string>] [[-CharacterSet] <string>] [[-MaxDepth] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Walks dictionaries, collections, and object properties and returns a stable
hierarchy without writing to the host. Compact style places scalar values
beside their labels. Expanded style gives scalar values their own nodes.
ASCII and Unicode connector sets are explicit and deterministic.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-InputObject` | `Object` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | Root object, dictionary, or collection to render. |
| `-RootLabel` | `String` | No | 2 | No | Root | Label for the root node. |
| `-Style` | `String` | No | 3 | No | Compact | Compact or Expanded scalar presentation. |
| `-CharacterSet` | `String` | No | 4 | No | Unicode | ASCII or Unicode branch connectors. |
| `-MaxDepth` | `Int32` | No | 5 | No | 12 | Maximum nested depth before an ellipsis node is emitted. |

### Inputs

- System.Object

### Outputs

- System.String

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Format-PoshUITree -InputObject $config -RootLabel Configuration
```

Formats a configuration object with Unicode connectors.

#### Example 2

```powershell
Format-PoshUITree -InputObject $plan -Style Expanded -CharacterSet ASCII
```

Formats scalar values as child nodes using ASCII connectors.

#### Example 3

```powershell
,@('api', 'worker') | Format-PoshUITree -RootLabel Services -MaxDepth 3
```

Formats a collection received from the pipeline.

### Notes

Circular references are reported as a visible circular marker.

## Show-PoshUITree

Displays nested objects and collections as a hierarchy

### Syntax

```powershell
Show-PoshUITree [-InputObject] <Object> [[-RootLabel] <string>] [[-Style] <string>] [[-CharacterSet] <string>] [[-MaxDepth] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Uses Format-PoshUITree to build the render model, then writes each line
through the shared PoshUI host boundary.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-InputObject` | `Object` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | Root object, dictionary, or collection to display. |
| `-RootLabel` | `String` | No | 2 | No | Root | Label for the root node. |
| `-Style` | `String` | No | 3 | No | Compact | Compact or Expanded scalar presentation. |
| `-CharacterSet` | `String` | No | 4 | No | Unicode | ASCII or Unicode connectors. |
| `-MaxDepth` | `Int32` | No | 5 | No | 12 | Maximum rendered nesting depth. |

### Inputs

- System.Object

### Outputs

- None

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Show-PoshUITree -InputObject $config
```

Displays a compact Unicode tree.

#### Example 2

```powershell
Show-PoshUITree -InputObject $plan -RootLabel Plan -Style Expanded
```

Displays an expanded plan hierarchy.

#### Example 3

```powershell
Show-PoshUITree -InputObject $results -CharacterSet ASCII -MaxDepth 5
```

Displays a bounded ASCII hierarchy.

### Notes

Off mode suppresses host output through Write-PoshUIHost.

## Format-PoshUICodeBlock

Formats source text as a stable code block

### Syntax

```powershell
Format-PoshUICodeBlock [-Text] <string> [[-StartLine] <int>] [[-Width] <int>] [-NoLineNumbers] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Returns source lines with optional one-based line numbers and deterministic
hard wrapping. Embedded newlines are preserved structurally as distinct
output lines. The command does not write to the host or depend on color.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Text` | `String` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | Source text or lines. Accepts pipeline input. |
| `-StartLine` | `Int32` | No | 2 | No | 1 | Number assigned to the first source line. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | 3 | No | 0 | Maximum content width. Zero disables wrapping. |
| `-NoLineNumbers` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Omits the line-number gutter. |

### Inputs

- System.String

### Outputs

- System.String

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Format-PoshUICodeBlock -Text 'Get-Process'
```

Formats one numbered source line.

#### Example 2

```powershell
Get-Content script.ps1 | Format-PoshUICodeBlock -StartLine 20
```

Formats pipeline text beginning at line 20.

#### Example 3

```powershell
Format-PoshUICodeBlock -Text $source -Width 40 -NoLineNumbers
```

Returns wrapped source without a number gutter.

### Notes

Wrapping counts terminal display columns and preserves ANSI and grapheme boundaries.

## Format-PoshUIDiff

Formats a line-oriented text diff

### Syntax

```powershell
Format-PoshUIDiff [-OldText] <string[]> [-NewText] <string[]> [[-ContextLines] <int>] [[-Width] <int>] [-NoLineNumbers] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Computes a longest-common-subsequence diff and emits context, removal, and
addition lines. Every state has a stable leading marker, so meaning never
depends on color. Optional wrapping retains that marker on continuations.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-OldText` | `String[]` | Yes | 1 | No |  | Original text or lines. |
| `-NewText` | `String[]` | Yes | 2 | No |  | Replacement text or lines. |
| `-ContextLines` | `Int32` | No | 3 | No | 3 | Unchanged lines retained around changes. Use zero for changed lines only. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | 4 | No | 0 | Maximum content width. Zero disables wrapping. |
| `-NoLineNumbers` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Omits old and new line-number gutters but retains state markers. |

### Inputs

- None

### Outputs

- System.String

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Format-PoshUIDiff -OldText 'old' -NewText 'new'
```

Returns one removal and one addition.

#### Example 2

```powershell
Format-PoshUIDiff -OldText $before -NewText $after -ContextLines 1
```

Retains one unchanged line around each change.

#### Example 3

```powershell
Format-PoshUIDiff -OldText $before -NewText $after -Width 60 -NoLineNumbers
```

Returns wrapped marker-only diff lines.

### Notes

The algorithm is intended for terminal-sized text, not very large files.

## Show-PoshUIDiff

Displays a line-oriented text diff

### Syntax

```powershell
Show-PoshUIDiff [-OldText] <string[]> [-NewText] <string[]> [[-ContextLines] <int>] [[-Width] <int>] [-NoLineNumbers] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |

| `-NewText` | `String[]` | Yes | 2 | No |  | Replacement text or lines. |
| `-ContextLines` | `Int32` | No | 3 | No | 3 | Unchanged lines retained around changes. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | 4 | No | 0 | Maximum content width. Zero disables wrapping. |
| `-NoLineNumbers` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Omits line-number gutters. |

### Inputs

- None

### Outputs

- None

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Show-PoshUIDiff -OldText $before -NewText $after
```

Displays a numbered diff.

#### Example 2

```powershell

```

Displays changed lines only.

#### Example 3

```powershell
Show-PoshUIDiff -OldText $before -NewText $after -Width 80 -NoLineNumbers
```

### Notes

Off mode suppresses host output through Write-PoshUIHost.

## New-PoshUIStepper

Creates an independent stepper or timeline model

### Syntax

```powershell
New-PoshUIStepper [[-Title] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Creates an in-memory model with its own mutable step collection. Multiple
models can be updated and rendered independently. It owns no cursor state
and performs no terminal writes.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Title` | `String` | No | 1 | No |  | Optional title rendered before the steps. |

### Inputs

- None

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
New-PoshUIStepper
```

Creates an untitled empty stepper.

#### Example 2

```powershell
New-PoshUIStepper -Title Deployment
```

Creates a titled deployment stepper.

#### Example 3

```powershell
$timeline = New-PoshUIStepper -Title 'Release timeline'
```

Stores an independent timeline model.

### Notes

The returned Steps list belongs only to the new instance.

## Add-PoshUIStep

Adds a stage to a stepper model

### Syntax

```powershell
Add-PoshUIStep [-Stepper] <psobject> [-Id] <string> [-Label] <string> [[-State] <string>] [[-Description] <string>] [[-Value] <Object>] [[-Timestamp] <datetime>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Adds one typed stage to the supplied independent model. Each stage has a
stable identifier, visible status, optional description, typed value, and
optional timestamp for timeline rendering.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Stepper` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | No |  | PoshUI.Stepper model to mutate. |
| `-Id` | `String` | Yes | 2 | No |  | Unique step identifier within the model. |
| `-Label` | `String` | Yes | 3 | No |  | Human-readable stage label. |
| `-State` | `String` | No | 4 | No | Pending | Pending, Active, Success, Failed, or Skipped. |
| `-Description` | `String` | No | 5 | No |  | Optional expanded-style detail. |
| `-Value` | `Object` | No | 6 | No |  | Optional typed consumer value retained on the stage. |
| `-Timestamp` | `Nullable`1` | No | 7 | No |  | Optional point in time shown in the render model. |

### Inputs

- None

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Add-PoshUIStep -Stepper $steps -Id build -Label Build
```

Adds a pending Build stage.

#### Example 2

```powershell
Add-PoshUIStep -Stepper $steps -Id test -Label Test -State Active -Description 'Running Pester'
```

Adds an active stage with detail.

#### Example 3

```powershell
Add-PoshUIStep -Stepper $timeline -Id deploy -Label Deployed -State Success -Timestamp (Get-Date) -Value $release
```

Adds a successful typed timeline event.

### Notes

Duplicate identifiers are rejected.

## Set-PoshUIStep

Updates a stage in a stepper model

### Syntax

```powershell
Set-PoshUIStep [-Stepper] <psobject> [-Id] <string> [[-State] <string>] [[-Label] <string>] [[-Description] <string>] [[-Value] <Object>] [[-Timestamp] <datetime>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Locates one stage by identifier and changes only explicitly supplied
fields. The model remains independent of every other stepper instance.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Stepper` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | No |  | PoshUI.Stepper model to mutate. |
| `-Id` | `String` | Yes | 2 | No |  | Identifier of the stage to update. |
| `-State` | `String` | No | 3 | No |  | Replacement stage state. |
| `-Label` | `String` | No | 4 | No |  | Replacement label. |
| `-Description` | `String` | No | 5 | No |  | Replacement expanded detail. |
| `-Value` | `Object` | No | 6 | No |  | Replacement typed consumer value. |
| `-Timestamp` | `Nullable`1` | No | 7 | No |  | Replacement timeline timestamp. |

### Inputs

- None

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Set-PoshUIStep -Stepper $steps -Id build -State Active
```

Marks Build active.

#### Example 2

```powershell
Set-PoshUIStep -Stepper $steps -Id build -State Success -Description 'Artifact ready'
```

Completes Build and replaces its detail.

#### Example 3

```powershell
Set-PoshUIStep -Stepper $timeline -Id deploy -Timestamp (Get-Date) -Value $result
```

Records typed timeline completion data.

### Notes

An unknown identifier is a terminating error.

## Format-PoshUIStepper

Formats a stepper or timeline model as composable lines

### Syntax

```powershell
Format-PoshUIStepper [-Stepper] <psobject> [[-Style] <string>] [[-CharacterSet] <string>] [[-TimestampFormat] <string>] [[-Width] <int>] [[-Overflow] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Returns a deterministic render model with visible state words and optional
timestamps. Icons supplement rather than replace state text. Compact style
emits one line per step; Expanded style includes descriptions.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Stepper` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | PoshUI.Stepper model to format. |
| `-Style` | `String` | No | 2 | No | Compact | Compact or Expanded presentation. |
| `-CharacterSet` | `String` | No | 3 | No | Unicode | ASCII or Unicode icons and connectors. |
| `-TimestampFormat` | `String` | No | 4 | No | yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss | Date and time format applied to stages with timestamps. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | 5 | No | 0 | Maximum terminal width. Zero uses the intrinsic width of the render model. |
| `-Overflow` | `String` | No | 6 | No | Wrap | Wraps logical lines or truncates them with an ellipsis at Width. |

### Inputs

- PoshUI.Stepper

### Outputs

- System.String

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Format-PoshUIStepper -Stepper $steps
```

Returns a compact Unicode render model.

#### Example 2

```powershell
$steps | Format-PoshUIStepper -Style Expanded
```

Returns descriptions beneath stage lines.

#### Example 3

```powershell
Format-PoshUIStepper -Stepper $timeline -CharacterSet ASCII -TimestampFormat 'HH:mm:ss' -Width 30 -Overflow Wrap
```

Returns an ASCII timeline with time values.

### Notes

The function is pure and does not mutate the supplied model.

## Show-PoshUIStepper

Displays a stepper or timeline model

### Syntax

```powershell
Show-PoshUIStepper [-Stepper] <psobject> [[-Style] <string>] [[-CharacterSet] <string>] [[-TimestampFormat] <string>] [[-Width] <int>] [[-Overflow] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Formats a model with Format-PoshUIStepper and writes every line through the
shared PoshUI host boundary. It does not claim or move the cursor.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Stepper` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | PoshUI.Stepper model to display. |
| `-Style` | `String` | No | 2 | No | Compact | Compact or Expanded presentation. |
| `-CharacterSet` | `String` | No | 3 | No | Unicode | ASCII or Unicode icons and connectors. |
| `-TimestampFormat` | `String` | No | 4 | No | yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss | Date and time format applied to stages with timestamps. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | 5 | No | 0 | Maximum terminal width. Zero uses the intrinsic render width. |
| `-Overflow` | `String` | No | 6 | No | Wrap | Wrap or Truncate behavior applied at Width. |

### Inputs

- PoshUI.Stepper

### Outputs

- None

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Show-PoshUIStepper -Stepper $steps
```

Displays a compact stepper.

#### Example 2


Displays stage descriptions.

#### Example 3

```powershell
Show-PoshUIStepper -Stepper $timeline -CharacterSet ASCII -TimestampFormat 'HH:mm' -Width 40
```

Off mode suppresses host output through Write-PoshUIHost.

## New-PoshUILiveRegion

Creates an independent live display region.

### Syntax

```powershell
New-PoshUILiveRegion [-Name] <string> [-Title <string>] [-Width <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Creates a typed in-memory model that coordinates independently keyed
dashboard, progress, spinner, log, and custom content. Creating a model
does not write to the terminal or mutate environment variables.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Name` | `String` | Yes | 1 | No |  | A diagnostic name for the region. |
| `-Title` | `String` | No | named | No |  | Optional text rendered before the keyed content. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | named | No | 0 | Maximum physical terminal width. Zero resolves the current terminal width<br>with one column reserved to prevent automatic wrapping. |

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
$region = New-PoshUILiveRegion -Name build
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
$region = New-PoshUILiveRegion -Name deploy -Title 'Deployment'
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
New-PoshUILiveRegion status | Format-PoshUILiveRegion
```

## Set-PoshUILiveRegionContent

Sets independently keyed content in a live region.

### Syntax

```powershell
Set-PoshUILiveRegionContent [-Region] <LiveRegion> [-Key] <string> [-Content] <string[]> [-Kind <string>] [-PassThru] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Adds or replaces one keyed content entry without writing to the terminal.
Existing keys retain their display order. The supplied region is the only
state mutated by this command.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Region` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | The live region returned by New-PoshUILiveRegion. |
| `-Key` | `String` | Yes | 2 | No |  | The stable identity used to add or replace the content. |
| `-Content` | `String[]` | Yes | 3 | No |  | One or more rendered text lines. |
| `-Kind` | `String` | No | named | No | Content | The semantic content kind. |
| `-PassThru` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Returns the updated region. |

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Set-PoshUILiveRegionContent $region build 'Compiling' -Kind Progress
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
$region | Set-PoshUILiveRegionContent -Key clock -Content '12:00' -Kind Dashboard
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
Set-PoshUILiveRegionContent $region worker @('Working', 'Please wait') -Kind Spinner -PassThru
```

```powershell
$region | Add-PoshUILiveRegionMessage -Message @('Step 1', 'Step 2')

```


#### Example 2

```powershell
$region | Show-PoshUILiveRegion
```


## Close-PoshUILiveRegion

Closes a live region and restores cursor visibility.

### Syntax

```powershell
Close-PoshUILiveRegion [-Region] <LiveRegion> [-Clear] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Releases terminal ownership and restores the cursor in a finally block.
Repeated calls are safe. By default, the last rendered snapshot remains in
the transcript.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Region` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | The live region to close. |
| `-Clear` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Clears the currently rendered rich-terminal lines before closing. |
| `-WhatIf` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No |  |  |
| `-Confirm` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No |  |  |

### Outputs

- None

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Close-PoshUILiveRegion $region
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
$region | Close-PoshUILiveRegion -Clear
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
try { Show-PoshUILiveRegion $region } finally { Close-PoshUILiveRegion $region }
```

## Invoke-PoshUILiveRegion

Runs work with guaranteed live-region cleanup.

### Syntax

```powershell
Invoke-PoshUILiveRegion [-Region] <LiveRegion> [-ScriptBlock] <scriptblock> [[-ArgumentList] <Object[]>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Invokes a script block with the supplied region and always closes the
region in a finally block. Cursor restoration therefore occurs after
success, cancellation exceptions, and other exceptions.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Region` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | No |  | The live region passed as the first script-block argument. |
| `-ScriptBlock` | `ScriptBlock` | Yes | 2 | No |  | Work to invoke while the region is active. |
| `-ArgumentList` | `Object[]` | No | 3 | No | @() | Optional arguments passed after the region. |

### Outputs

- System.Object

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Invoke-PoshUILiveRegion $region { param($live) Show-PoshUILiveRegion $live }
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
$result = Invoke-PoshUILiveRegion $region { param($live, $name) $name } -ArgumentList build
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
Invoke-PoshUILiveRegion $region { throw 'Stopped' }
```

## New-PoshUISelectionItem

Creates a typed searchable-selection item.

### Syntax

```powershell
New-PoshUISelectionItem [-Label] <string> [-Value] <Object> [-Preview <string>] [-Keywords <string[]>] [-Disabled] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Associates a display label with an arbitrary typed value, optional preview
text, search keywords, and enabled state. The value is retained without
string conversion.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Label` | `String` | Yes | 1 | No |  | Text displayed and searched for the item. |
| `-Value` | `Object` | Yes | 2 | No |  | The value returned when this item is accepted. |
| `-Preview` | `String` | No | named | No |  | Optional detail displayed while the item is selected. |
| `-Keywords` | `String[]` | No | named | No | @() | Additional terms considered by filtering. |
| `-Disabled` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Prevents navigation to and acceptance of the item. |

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
New-PoshUISelectionItem -Label Production -Value 3
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
New-PoshUISelectionItem QA ([uri]'https://qa.example.test') -Preview 'Quality assurance'
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
New-PoshUISelectionItem Legacy old -Keywords archive,retired -Disabled
```

## Find-PoshUISelectionItem

Filters selection items by an incremental query.

### Syntax

```powershell
Find-PoshUISelectionItem [-Item] <SelectionItem[]> [[-Query] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Returns items whose label or keywords contain every whitespace-separated
query token. Matching is case-insensitive and preserves source order and
disabled items.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Item` | `PSObject[]` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | Typed items to filter. |
| `-Query` | `String` | No | 2 | No |  | The incremental search text. Empty text returns every item. |

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Find-PoshUISelectionItem -Item $items -Query prod
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
$items | Find-PoshUISelectionItem -Query 'east api'
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
Find-PoshUISelectionItem $items ''
```

## New-PoshUISearchSelection

Creates an independent searchable-selection model.

### Syntax

```powershell
New-PoshUISearchSelection [-Item] <SelectionItem[]> [[-Prompt] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Creates a typed state model containing source items, filtered items, query,
navigation position, and acceptance or cancellation state. It performs no
terminal input or output.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Item` | `PSObject[]` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | Items created by New-PoshUISelectionItem. |
| `-Prompt` | `String` | No | 2 | No | Select an item | Text displayed above the query and choices. |

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
$selection = New-PoshUISearchSelection -Item $items
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
$selection = $items | New-PoshUISearchSelection -Prompt 'Environment'
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
New-PoshUISearchSelection $items 'Choose a target' | Format-PoshUISearchSelection
```

## Update-PoshUISearchSelection

Applies one input action to a searchable-selection model.

### Syntax

```powershell
Update-PoshUISearchSelection [-Selection] <SearchSelection> [-Action] <string> [-Character <string>] [-PassThru] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Updates query, filtering, navigation, cancellation, or acceptance state.
Navigation wraps and skips disabled entries. The supplied model is the only
state mutated.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Selection` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | The searchable-selection model to update. |
| `-Action` | `String` | Yes | 2 | No |  | The input action to apply. |
| `-Character` | `String` | No | named | No |  | A character appended when Action is Append. |
| `-PassThru` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Returns the updated selection. |

### Outputs

- System.Management.Automation.PSCustomObject

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Update-PoshUISearchSelection $selection Next
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
$selection | Update-PoshUISearchSelection -Action Append -Character p
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
Update-PoshUISearchSelection $selection Accept -PassThru
```

## Format-PoshUISearchSelection

Formats a searchable selection without terminal effects.

### Syntax

```powershell
Format-PoshUISearchSelection [-Selection] <SearchSelection> [-NoPreview] [-Width <int>] [-Overflow <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Returns stable plain-text lines for the prompt, incremental query, filtered
choices, empty state, and optional selected-item preview.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Selection` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | The searchable-selection model to format. |
| `-NoPreview` | `SwitchParameter` | No | named | No | False | Suppresses optional preview text. |
| `-Width` | `Int32` | No | named | No | 0 | Maximum output width. Zero, the default, disables width limiting. |
| `-Overflow` | `String` | No | named | No | Truncate | Truncates long lines with an ellipsis or wraps them at Width without<br>splitting a grapheme cluster. |

### Outputs

- System.String

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
Format-PoshUISearchSelection $selection
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
$lines = $selection | Format-PoshUISearchSelection -NoPreview
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
Format-PoshUISearchSelection $selection -Width 24 -Overflow Wrap
```

## Select-PoshUIItem

Interactively selects and returns one typed value.

### Syntax

```powershell
Select-PoshUIItem [-Selection] <SearchSelection> [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Description

Displays a searchable selection, reads incremental keyboard input, and
returns the accepted item's original value. Redirected or unavailable input
returns null immediately without reading from Console. Escape cancels.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Position | Pipeline | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Selection` | `PSObject` | Yes | 1 | true (ByValue) |  | The searchable-selection model to run. |

### Outputs

- System.Object

### Examples

#### Example 1

```powershell
$value = Select-PoshUIItem $selection
```

#### Example 2

```powershell
$items | New-PoshUISearchSelection | Select-PoshUIItem
```

#### Example 3

```powershell
if ($null -eq (Select-PoshUIItem $selection)) { 'Cancelled' }
```
